heading.en: Is it fat or sugar that is burning?

hook.en: By measuring only how much CO₂ an organism gives out and how much O₂ it takes in, we can tell whether it is respiring carbohydrate, fat or protein.

title.en: Calculate the net ATP of aerobic respiration and state its assumptions.
Explain why respiration is an amphibolic pathway.

say.en: By measuring only how much CO 2 an organism gives out and how much O 2 it takes in, we can tell whether it is respiring carbohydrate, fat or protein. In this lesson: Calculate the net ATP of aerobic respiration and state its assumptions.
Explain why respiration is an amphibolic pathway.
Calculate RQ for different substrates.

body.en: The net ATP from one glucose can be calculated only on certain assumptions: there is a sequential, orderly pathway (glycolysis, TCA cycle, ETS); NADH made in glycolysis is transferred into the mitochondria and undergoes oxidative phosphorylation; none of the intermediates are used to make other compounds; and only glucose is respired. Under these assumptions there can be a net gain of 38 ATP molecules during aerobic respiration of one glucose. Such assumptions are not really valid in a living system, since all pathways work simultaneously, so the *balance sheet* is a useful exercise rather than an exact figure.

say.en: Link reaction: 2 NADH equals 6 ATP.
Krebs: 6 NADH 18 plus 2 FADH 2 4 plus 2 GTP 2 equals 24.
Total equals 8 plus 6 plus 24 equals 38 ATP.

narration.en: Let us draw up the ATP balance sheet, see how other foods enter the pathway, and calculate RQ.

say.en: Draw a table: for each stage, count NADH, FADH₂ and the ATP made directly, then convert them all to ATP.
Glycolysis: 2 NADH and 2 ATP, which is 8 ATP. Link reaction: 2 NADH, which is 6 ATP.
Krebs cycle, two turns: 6 NADH, 2 FADH₂ and 2 GTP, which is 24 ATP. The total is 38 ATP per glucose.

text.en: Real cells: all pathways run together

say.en: Fats and proteins also feed the pathway, and its intermediates are drawn off to build molecules. Breakdown plus synthesis: an amphibolic pathway.
The respiratory quotient is the volume of CO₂ given out divided by the volume of O₂ taken in.
For tripalmitin, 102 CO₂ for 145 O₂ gives 0.70. Glucose gives 1, and oxygen-rich malic acid gives 1.33.
Let us draw up the ATP balance sheet, see how other foods enter the pathway, and calculate RQ.

caption.en: RQ = volume of CO2 released / volume of O2 used. It depends on the substrate: about 1 for carbohydrates, about 0.7 for fats (which need more oxygen), about 0.9 for proteins and more than 1 for organic acids such as malic acid. In anaerobic respiration no O2 is used, so the RQ is infinite.
caption.kn: RQ = ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾದ CO2 / ಬಳಸಿದ O2. ಕಾರ್ಬೋಹೈಡ್ರೇಟ್‌ಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 1, ಕೊಬ್ಬಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 0.7, ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 0.9, ಸಾವಯವ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳಿಗೆ 1 ಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು. ಅವಾಯುವಿಕ ಉಸಿರಾಟದಲ್ಲಿ RQ ಅನಂತ.

body.en: Fats are broken down to glycerol and fatty acids; fatty acids are degraded to acetyl CoA, and glycerol is converted to PGAL. Proteins are degraded by proteases to amino acids, which after deamination enter at some stage of the Krebs cycle or as pyruvate or acetyl CoA. When the body needs to synthesise fatty acids, acetyl CoA is withdrawn from the pathway. Because the respiratory pathway is involved in both breakdown (catabolism) and synthesis (anabolism), it is an *amphibolic pathway*. The respiratory quotient (RQ) is the ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed. It is 1 for carbohydrates, less than 1 for fats (about 0.7 for tripalmitin) and about 0.9 for proteins.

points.en: Organic acids, which are oxygen-rich, give RQ above 1.

problem.en: Calculate the RQ of tripalmitin from: 2 C₅₁H₉₈O₆ + 145 O₂ → 102 CO₂ + 98 H₂O + energy.

steps.en: CO₂ evolved = 102 molecules; O₂ consumed = 145 molecules.
RQ = 0.703 ≈ 0.7, less than 1, as expected for a fat.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Calculate the RQ of tripalmitin from: 2 C₅₁H₉₈O₆ + 145 O₂ → 102 CO₂ + 98 H₂O + energy.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Calculate the RQ of tripalmitin from: 2 C 51H 98O 6 plus 145 O 2 gives 102 CO 2 plus 98 H 2O plus energy.
CO 2 evolved equals 102 molecules; O 2 consumed equals 145 molecules.
RQ equals 102 divided by 145.
RQ equals 0.703 is approximately 0.7, less than 1, as expected for a fat.
So the answer is RQ is approximately 0.7.

problem.en: Calculate the RQ of malic acid: C₄H₆O₅ + 3 O₂ → 4 CO₂ + 3 H₂O.

steps.en: RQ is above 1 because the organic acid already contains much oxygen.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Calculate the RQ of malic acid: C₄H₆O₅ + 3 O₂ → 4 CO₂ + 3 H₂O.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Calculate the RQ of malic acid: C 4H 6O 5 plus 3 O 2 gives 4 CO 2 plus 3 H 2O.
CO 2 evolved equals 4; O 2 consumed equals 3.
RQ equals 4 divided by 3 equals 1.33.
RQ is above 1 because the organic acid already contains much oxygen.
So the answer is RQ is approximately 1.33.
